These are estimates from my prior knowledge of NAS-Bench-201 behavior. I did not run any queries against the benchmark.

Reasoning I applied:
- Removing or replacing an edge matters less when the condition already puts a weak op on that edge, or when other edges still carry the signal.
- Conv ops on edges near the output matter most, and effects usually shrink when a parallel path already supplies strong features.
- Many interactions are small or inconsistent across the three datasets, so N is the default.
